title: Cross-Loss Influence Functions to Explain Deep Network Representations
findings: The study found that the proposed CLIF method could identify seemingly unrelated training data that significantly influenced model bias. Specifically, it uncovered that sentences associating religious concepts (e.g., 'Jewish self-hatred', 'Islamophobia') with unpleasantness were highly influential in creating a racial bias against African-American names. This was due to the model learning a stronger correlation between African-American names and these religious terms than between European-American names and the same terms, revealing a non-obvious, second-order source of bias.

measurement_description: Discovering indirect racial bias mediated through associations with religious concepts. A custom Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT) was constructed to measure the association between racial names (African-American, European-American) and religious terms (from Judaism and Islam) that were linked to unpleasant concepts in the training data.
